+    "dangerous": [
+      "Alcohol (Both substances potentiate the ataxia and sedation caused by the other and can lead to unexpected loss of consciousness at high doses. Place the affected individual in the recovery position to prevent vomit aspiration from excess. Additionally, CNS depression can lead to difficulty breathing. Avoid on anything higher than 1st plateau.)",
+      "AMT",
+      "GHB/GBL (Both substances cause ataxia and bring a risk of vomiting and unconsciousness. If the individual falls unconscious while under the influence there is a severe risk of vomit aspiration if they are not placed in the recovery position. This combination is hard to predict)",
+      "Lithium (There is a risk of serotonin syndrome when combining Lithium with DXM.)",
+      "MAOIs (High risk of serotonin syndrome)",
+      "MDMA",
+      "Mephedrone (Risk of serotonin syndrome as both drugs raise serotonin levels. In addition to concerns of high blood pressure and unnecessary strain on the heart. As well as potentially causing anxiety and greater physical discomfort due to the combination.)",
+      "Opioids (CNS depression, difficult breathing, heart issues, hepatoxic, just very unsafe combination all around. Additionally if one takes DXM, their tolerance of opiates goes down slightly, thus causing additional synergistic effects.)",
+      "PCP",
+      "SSRIs (High risk of serotonin syndrome.)",
+      "Tramadol"
+    ],
+    "unsafe": [
+      "2C-T-x compounds",
+      "5-MeO-xxT tryptamines (Little information exists about this combination.)",
+      "Amphetamines (Both substances raise heart rate, in extreme cases, panic attacks caused by these drugs have led to more serious heart issues.)",
+      "Cocaine (Both substances raise heart rate, in extreme cases, panic attacks caused by these drugs have led to more serious heart issues)",
+      "Diphenhydramine (The combination is reported to reduce the side effects of each drug and potentiate many of the recreational effects. There is a significant risk of serotonin syndrome, increased delirium, CNS depression, cognitive inhibition, risk of physical injury, hyperthermia, mania, paranoia, and psychosis, especially at higher dosages. There is an additional concern of tachycardia, hypertension, and in extreme cases, heart failure. Diphenhydramine is reported to inhibit the CYP2D6 enzyme which can increase levels of DXM. Medical dosages are not reported to be a concern. Caution is strongly recommended with this combination.)",
+      "DOx compounds (The DOx class as psychedelic stimulants have the potential to mask the effects of DXM and could lead to redosing to an unsafe level. DXM can also potentiate DOx resulting in an unpleasantly intense experience.)",
+      "MXE (There is a risk of serotonin syndrome when combining DXM with MXE, due to DXM and MXE both being SRI’s. MXE and DXM having notable affinities for the serotonin transporter.)",
+      "NBOMe compounds",
+      "Pregabalin (Pregabalin and DXM may increase each other’s effects such as inhibition, dizziness, sedation. At higher doses this can lead to unexpected loss of consciousness. Both drugs have seizure concerns which is greatly increased in combination.)"
+    ],
+    "caution": [
+      "Benzodiazepines (Small doses of benzos can end a bad trip, but both substances potentiate the ataxia and sedation caused by the other and this can lead to unexpected loss of consciousness at high doses. While unconscious, vomit aspiration is a risk if not placed in the recovery position.)",
+      "Caffeine (High doses of caffeine can potentially exacerbate anxiety, especially during a dissociative experience, due to its stimulating effects. This combination might also lead to physical discomfort. However, individual responses to caffeine can vary significantly, often influenced by factors like habitual versus occasional usage.)"
+    ]

+    "addiction_liability": "Moderate abuse potential with documented cases of psychological addiction. Some users develop compulsive daily use patterns and report difficulty discontinuing. Physical addiction comparable to alcohol or benzodiazepines does not typically develop.",
+    "dependence_liability": "Physical dependence develops with chronic use, producing withdrawal symptoms similar to antidepressant discontinuation syndrome. Reported withdrawal effects include fatigue, apathy, flashbacks, constipation, insomnia, nightmares, anhedonia, impaired memory, attention deficits, and decreased libido. Tolerance develops with regular use, requiring increased doses for equivalent effects.",
-      "ld50": "",
+      "ld50": "Estimated lethal dose in humans approximately 2,200-2,500 mg, though fatalities have occurred across a wide range (2,500-20,000 mg reported).",
-      "other": ""
+      "other": "Neurotoxicity remains controversial. While rat studies did not demonstrate Olney's lesions from oral DXM, adolescent exposure impaired adult learning in animal models. Heavy chronic users report persistent deficits in episodic memory, learning ability, visual processing, and abstract language comprehension lasting months after cessation. Some users develop irreversible permanent tolerance, potentially indicating cumulative neurotoxic damage."

+      "psychosis": "High doses and extended use (7+ days of heavy use) associated with lasting delusional, paranoid, and psychotic ideation persisting for days to months. Toxic psychosis may develop with frequent high-dose use. Paranoid ideation and delusions (persecution, mind-reading, divine contact) commonly reported at third plateau and above.",
+      "self_harm": "Risk of accidental injury and self-harm during high-dose experiences. Functional anesthetization at fourth plateau may fail to prevent acting out in response to hallucinations and delusions, leading to dangerous behavior.",
+      "seizure": "Seizures reported at high doses and during overdose. Fever combined with seizures can cause brain cell death.",
+      "other": [
+        "Respiratory depression is a rare but serious side effect, becoming significant at overdose levels",
+        "Dangerously elevated body temperature (hyperthermia) at high doses",
+        "Overdose complications include severely elevated heart rate and blood pressure, urinary retention, and rhabdomyolysis",
+        "Multi-ingredient product misuse poses severe risk: acetaminophen causes fatal liver damage, chlorpheniramine causes seizures, loss of consciousness, and death at recreational DXM doses",
+        "Prolonged depersonalization and derealization may persist for days following use",
+        "Chronic use associated with depression and persistent mood disturbances"
+      ]
